methodology: A series of cyclic polymer additives were synthesized via ring-expansion cationic polymerization, and their surface segregation behavior was investigated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis under different conditions (molecular weight, pendant length). Additionally, the effect of perfluoroalkyl pendant groups on antifouling properties was studied.
research_objective: To develop a novel cyclic polymer additive platform for enhancing surface segregation and to demonstrate its potential as an alternative to existing biomedical coatings.

key_findings.finding: Cyclic polymer additives with no chain ends show enhanced surface segregation compared to linear polymers when blended with polyurethane.
The addition of perfluoroalkyl pendant groups to the cyclic additive reveals a promising antifouling effect in plasma protein adsorption.
Surface segregation efficiency is significantly higher for cyclic polymers compared to linear ones.
Ring-expansion technique is commercially advantageous due to its lack of high dilution reaction requirement.
Cyclic polymer additives have higher surface segregation efficiencies than linear polymer additives.
Synthesis of polymers with cyclic topology using different chain and pendant lengths
Investigation of additive-modified polymer surface functionality through cationic polymerization of vinyl ether derivatives

properties.context: A computational study on the surface segregation of polymers with cyclic topologies was performed previously by Wu and Fredrickson [26].
A study on additives with different chain lengths was also conducted using poly(ethyl vinyl ether) (pEVE).
The interaction between the chain ends of the polymer architecture and the surface plays an important role in functional diversification.
A polymer-blended TPU film containing 1 wt% additive was prepared using a solvent-casting method.

Unlike other modification methods, this technique is simple and does not Polymer blend require any complex modeling or additional processing steps for surface modification. Most surface segregation Surface segregation studies are based on the interaction between the chain ends of the additive and bulk polymer at the surface. Additive However, additives with cyclic topologies without chain ends have not been used. In this study, an additive Cyclic polymer platform with cyclic topology without a chain end was designed for surface modification. A series of cyclic Ring-expansion cationic polymerization additives were synthesized via ring-expansion cationic polymerization. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy anal- ysis of the cyclic polymer additive showed approximately 1.5 times higher surface segregation than the linear polymer when blended wit n cationic polymerization. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy anal- ysis of the cyclic polymer additive showed approximately 1.5 times higher surface segregation than the linear polymer when blended with polyurethane. In addition, the surface segregation behavior depending on the molecular weight and pendant length of the cyclic polymer additive was investigated. Moreover, the monomer, allyl vinyl ether, enabled the addition of functional groups to the cyclic additive and the addition of per- fluoroalkyl pendant groups was performed, revealing a promising antifouling effect in the adsorption of a plasma protein. The high performance and versatility of the cyclic architectural polymer additives extend the scope of the surface segregation field and can replace existing biomedical coatings. 1.
